notes.title: Ars Notoria Playtest Has Ended – See You Next Time!
notes.notes: [p]Thank you to everyone who joined and supported this round of the <Ars Notoria>[b] [/b]Playtest! The test has officially ended at 10:00 UTC.[/p][p]Over the past days, we’ve received a wealth of valuable feedback and suggestions from the community. Every play session, every comment, has been a driving force for us to improve the game. Our development team will carefully review and absorb these insights as we continue refining [i]Ars Notoria[/i][b] [/b]toward a more complete and polished experience.[/p][p]This is not the end, but the beginning of the next stage. We look forward to reuniting with you in future tests and growing [i]Ars Notoria[/i][b] [/b]together![/p][p][/p][p]————————————————————————————————[/p][p]Hello everyone, we are the development team of Ars Notoria! We sincerely thank you for your continued attention and support for the game. After a month of dedicated polishing, we’re excited to present to you the brand-new [b]Version 0.3.2.0[/b] of Ars Notoria![/p][p]From smoother loading and performance improvements to an expanded Faction Management system, this update brings new vitality into the world of Ars Notoria. We’ve laid the foundation, but what truly brings the game to life is your creativity and feedback.[/p][p][/p][p]Whether you’re a long-time player who has accompanied us on this journey or a newcomer stepping into adventure for the first time, now is the perfect moment to experience Ars Notoria. We warmly invite you to join us—build, explore, and share your unique experiences. Your feedback just might shape the next version![/p][p][/p][h3]How to Participate:[/h3][p]If you’ve participated in a previous Ars Notoria playtest, you can download and launch the new build from your library. [/p][p]If this is your first time, simply click the “Request Access” button on the Steam store page — you’ll receive an email notification once you’ve been added to the playtest.[/p][p][img notes.title: Building in Ars Notoria
notes.notes:
[p]Hi everyone,[/p][p]Since the start of testing, we’ve made significant updates to the building system in [i][b]Ars Notoria[/b][/i], and in this dev log we’d like to share its current state and walk you through the progress so far.[/p][p]Building is one of the core systems in the game and is available from the very beginning. It provides essential benefits for your character, ranging from simple shelters and campfires to tools for harvesting and processing resources, and eventually sturdy dwellings and larger structures. As you gather your first materials like wood and stone, you’ll gradually unlock new building recipes and expand your options.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/20cdfc9648c097a6d2b6ec5fa1151634056e7b09.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’ve prepared two interface options for the Building Menu: [b]Radial[/b] and [b]Grid[/b], so you can choose whichever feels more convenient. The radial menu follows the classic survival building style, with categories and sub-menus where you can browse available parts. The grid menu offers a more condensed layout, replacing multiple sub-menus with a single page that displays a much larger number of recipes at once. You can freely switch between these two modes at any time in the settings.[/p][p]Currently, there are six main categories available in the building system:[/p][olist][*][p][b]Encampment[/b] – the first category to unlock, offering elements for temporary shelters such as tents, bedding, campfires, and simple wooden defenses.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Construction[/b] – includes the core pieces for building houses, from foundations, walls, and roofs to doors, windows, and other structural parts.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Furniture[/b] – provides all types of furnishings for your home, ranging from chairs and tables to cupboards and decorative stands.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Harvesting[/b] – contains equipment for gathering, processing, and storing the resources you find during exploration.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Production[/b] – features workbenches and tools for crafting advanced equipment, including weapons, armor, jewelry, and more.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Farming[/b] – lets you plant trees, bushes, and flowers, as well as construct a variety of outdoor utilities.[/p][/*][/olist][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/809545fe851ba563db4914cd1c17734fe9c9ab9c.jpg"][/img][/p][p]At the start of the game, most resources are gathered manually with tools like the axe, pickaxe, or sickle. As you progress, however, you can construct advanced harvesting and processing equipment to gradually automate the entire process.[/p][p]Basic processing tools, such as the [b]Circular Saw[/b] or [b]Bloomery[/b], can be connected to [b]Auto-Loaders[/b], which pull raw materials directly from your global storage and feed them into the machines. Once processing is complete, the loaders return the refined resources back to storage. In addition, you can build [b]Auto-Harvesters[/b], which automatically collect raw resources from deposits within a large radius.[/p][p]By combining these tools, you can set up full [b]resource production chains[/b] that supply everything needed for building while you focus on exploring the world.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/e6a05dca567d358454f7469f3906350505033ee7.jpg"][/img][/p][p]With resource chains in place, gathering and processing materials becomes far more efficient, giving you the freedom to focus on expanding your settlement. Once you have the necessary supplies, the next step is placing building parts to begin shaping your homes and settlements. To make this easier, the building system features a [b]grid-snapping mechanic[/b] that automatically aligns selected parts to compatible structures. For example, foundations include snap points for walls and stairs, while walls have slots for windows, doors, and roof modules. This helps keep your constructions organized and stable, while also speeding up the entire building process.[/p][p]We’ve recently expanded the range of available snapping options: foundations can now be aligned with flat ground modules, and fences can now snap to grids on both foundations and ground modules. Looking ahead, we’ll continue refining snapping behavior, while also adding an option for free placement. This will allow you to ignore grids entirely and even overlap certain structures, giving you much greater freedom in how you design your settlements.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/f72a4e13fe305c8b908baf70931420d5f61bab5f.jpg"][/img][/p][p]To further improve building part placement, we added a [b]Quick Menu[/b], which can be opened by aiming at a structure and pressing the [b]Q[/b] key. This menu provides several useful options, such as moving a part to another location, dismantling it to salvage resources (returning 100% of the materials used), or toggling the display radius for resource processing and automation tools.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/3fa426c072784134841c3a0a3ff5119047f9cc68.jpg"][/img][/p][p]One of the latest additions to the building system is [b]Basements[/b]. They begin with an entrance module placed on a foundation, which leads underground into a cellar. From there, you can expand further by constructing additional modules, creating extra storage space and opening up new possibilities for how you design your buildings.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/9645bfca17e7ec6ec0dc45522985661823f446f6.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’ve also introduced [b]Fortifications[/b] in the most recent update, allowing you to defend your encampment with palisade walls, gates, and towers. Unlike other building parts, these defenses are unlocked by completing a quest in the Training Camp. Fortifications provide protection against enemy ambushes, and later on you’ll be able to assign faction members as guards to man the towers and gates, keeping your settlement safe even when you’re away.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/4193c9e9042fb6f55feb7e1466420c33520d872d.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Storage Platforms[/b] are one of the features we added based on your feedback to make organizing resources more efficient. Each platform can hold up to four storage containers of any type, greatly increasing capacity, and they can even be stacked vertically to save space in your settlement. Storage Platforms are found in the Carpenter building category and require access to lumber and basic carpenter’s tools to unlock.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/0c063bbdcbb905d64460793a95f39843cd52abbd.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Efficiency of harvesting and production buildings can be increased by researching [b]Technologies[/b], unlocked after making the Engineer’s Workbench. Research provides many advantages, which makes setting up your settlement easier. For example, Auto-Loaders can be upgraded to support connection with multiple harvesting tools at once, which is great for optimizing the settlement layout and much more efficient than using a separate loader for each processing tool.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/14e0baff8029b2c459e2861c94fb7c7a41920274.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Last but not least, some building parts support advanced customization. You can apply paints and choose from a variety of patterns for elements such as tents, banners, and walls. In future updates, we plan to expand the number of parts that support these options and add new utilities to make customization even more convenient.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]Thank you for checking out this dev log! We appreciate your support and can’t wait to see how you build and customize your settlements in [i]Ars Notoria[/i].[/p]

notes.title: Dev Log 0.3.1 | We Heard You
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone![/p][p]We’re excited to share update 0.3.1, which brings a variety of improvements, balance tweaks, and bug fixes inspired by your feedback from previous testing stages. Huge thanks to everyone who joined the playtests and took the time to report issues and share suggestions. Your feedback plays a key role in how the game evolves.[/p][p][/p][p]In this dev log, we’ll highlight the main changes included in the new version. Let’s take a look![/p][p][/p][h3]Exploration[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/55e21d6e1a17675f42ead0edad69c9e9e2619b77.jpg"][/img][/p][p]One of the main areas we’re focusing on is exploration. We want every journey through the world to feel rewarding, and this update brings several new features to help with that:[/p][list][*][p][b]Aspects[/b] – ancient stone tablets infused with dormant magic. Each one you find permanently increases one of your character’s core attributes.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Gifts[/b] – special items that can be given to key characters in the Training Camp. They help increase approval, which can further unlock helpful bonuses.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Unique resources[/b] – rare deposits like gemstones, ornamental stones, or metal shards. These can be used for crafting things like jewelry and artifacts. Unlike common resources, which appear in many places, unique resources only exist in one fixed location. This makes discovering new areas especially valuable. Right now, these can be found only in dungeons, but more types are planned in future updates, including some in the open world.[/p][/*][*][p][b]New rare items, crafting recipes, and artifacts[/b] – hidden in the world, waiting to be discovered.[/p][/*][/list][p]We’ve also added new locations and made adjustments to some existing ones. A few now feature hidden cellars or small layout changes that reward exploration.[/p][p][/p][h3]Dungeons[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/7175c48635f7f9e0cfcab3070f94fae7f48bd354.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Previously, dungeons were packed with enemies but often felt underwhelming in terms of rewards. To make them worthwhile, we've introduced several types of treasure rooms that now appear at the end of all dungeons. These can include [b]Ancient Shrines[/b], [b]Burial Sites[/b], [b]Smuggler Stashes[/b], or [b]Mage Hideouts[/b], each offering special loot like Aspects, Gifts, unique resources, and rare items.[/p][p]We've also made some balancing tweaks: the maximum enemy level has been lowered in dungeons closer to the starting area, and enemy spawns have been slightly adjusted overall to improve pacing and challenge.[/p][p][/p][h3]Resources[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/ff1f60be2375fa94ba7eead220c2db41b8f314f9.png"][/img][/p][p]One of the most significant changes in this update concerns resource harvesting. Previously, each resource required a specific harvesting tool and did not provide skill experience if the wrong tool was used. Combined with the need for nine different tool types, this system was quite cumbersome. Now, tools are divided into two categories: [b]Essential[/b] and [b]Specialized[/b]. Essential tools include [b]Axe[/b], [b]Pickaxe[/b], and [b]Sickle[/b], which are sufficient to gather all resource types efficiently. Specialized tools remain in the game but are optional and provide minor bonuses to harvesting efficiency if you want the best results. Harvesting skill experience is now always granted in full regardless of the tool used. Additionally, crafting harvesting tools is no longer required to unlock processing equipment.[/p][p]Trees and plants now have a chance to drop seeds from the start of the game without needing specific abilities. These abilities will still increase the drop chance.[/p][p]Alongside new unique resources, a new processed resource called Ceramics has been introduced. Ceramics have a different crafting mechanic compared to other processed resources and are used in some building part recipes.[/p][p]We also made various quality of life improvements:[/p][list][*][p]Auto-equipping and manual resource harvesting work better.[/p][/*][*][p]Picking up resource pieces and other objects has been made easier.[/p][/*][*][p]Small shrubs can now be harvested directly without chopping.[/p][/*][*][p]Plants such as fibers and herbs grow closer together, making gathering more efficient.[/p][/*][*][p]Wood branches no longer appear on the minimap, reducing clutter.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Ambushes[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/8a0676e3f396c4636675c0e559d75504a33b20ed.jpg"][/img][/p][p]In earlier versions, enemies mostly kept to themselves unless you wandered directly into their territory. That’s changed. While exploring the open world, you can now be ambushed by roaming enemies. The type and strength of the attackers depend on the region you're in.[/p][p]Ambushes are more frequent at night, so think twice before heading out after dark. They’re active on Normal and Survival difficulties, with a higher rate on Survival. Sandbox players can rest easy, ambushes are disabled in that mode, so you can enjoy a more peaceful experience focused on building and crafting, if you prefer.[/p][p][/p][h3]Magic[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/8177bfa05e6c0690c6a577d784e3c3af9e57faf0.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Another key area we want to improve is the magic system. It was originally designed to support weapon combat skills with a hybrid approach, but we are now working to make pure caster playthroughs more viable. In this update, we added two new equipment sets specifically for mages: [b]Forsworn[/b] and [b]Apprentice[/b]. Newly introduced jewelry such as rings, amulets, and medallions also provide valuable bonuses to magic users.[/p][p]We included new magic types, [b]Shield[/b] and [b]Barrier[/b], that add protection for mages, helping them better withstand enemy attacks. Various balance changes have been made, including more than doubling spell damage, significantly buffing summons, and improving their attack range and targeting. Enemies will now prioritize nearby targets, focusing mostly on summons to keep the caster safer.[/p][p]Looking ahead, we plan to make mages a fully standalone class with their own skill and class trees. This will complement existing Magic Arts perks and Sigils, further enhancing their power and flexibility.[/p][h3][/h3][h3]Recipe Unlocks[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/3e5db2ebb594dfe5ec26011c4c28541d2b2796dd.png"][/img][/p][p]We’ve completely reworked how crafting and building recipes are unlocked. In previous versions, many recipes were hidden behind nested unlocks, where certain parts only became available after building others. This system was often confusing and hard to follow.[/p][p]Now, we’ve removed those nested requirements. Recipes are unlocked simply by collecting the relevant resource types or by constructing the appropriate workbenches for more advanced items.[/p][p]The updated unlock structure is also fully integrated into the in-game guide. At any time, you can open the guide to see which resources unlock specific building parts. You can also click on any item listed to craft or build it directly from the guide, without having to dig through menus. This should make the whole progression system much clearer and easier to use.[/p][p][/p][h3]Guide[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/3ebff4f27d9048181b9a854155d39206b41edeab.png"][/img][/p][p]We’ve added a new in-game guide that not only explains the updated recipe unlock system but also provides tutorials and breakdowns of key gameplay mechanics. It’s designed to help both new and returning players get a better understanding of how things work. The guide is always accessible from the Pause menu or by pressing the default shortcut key “G”.[/p][p][/p][h3]Building[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/c8ee6a6da8f41b6d5b331c3c476bc6ebc7ee630c.png"][/img][/p][p]The building system has received a wide range of improvements. New build parts have been added, and equipment has been unlocked for additional professions like [b]Mason[/b] and [b]Jeweler[/b]. Other professions, such as [b]Potter[/b] and [b]Carpenter[/b], also gain access to new tools.[/p][p]Stone structures and buildable [b]Basements[/b] are now available once Mason tools are unlocked. Basement modules can be combined to expand your home underground.[/p][p]All fences and gates have been made modular and now snap to placement grids on foundations and flat ground, making them easier to position. Foundation placement on flat ground also benefits from a grid system.[/p][p]Furniture variations are now handled as style options when placing a build part, rather than being listed separately in the build menu. This makes navigating furniture options more convenient.[/p][p]We've updated alignment logic for all house-building elements, fixing previous issues that sometimes caused misalignment or small visual gaps.[/p][p]Another new feature is [b]Camp Fortification[/b]. You can now defend your settlement using palisade walls, gates, walkways, and towers.[/p][p]Numerous bug fixes have also been made to improve overall building stability and behavior.[/p][p][/p][h3]Crafting[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/4d6b9eaf6143b8aa45ce688d5f11710ca8ebe251.png"][/img][/p][p]The crafting system received a number of additions and improvements. Jewelry crafting is now available, including [b]Rings[/b], [b]Amulets[/b], and [b]Medallions[/b], which require unique materials to unlock and make.[/p][p]Several new equipment sets have also been added, along with side quests related to their discovery.[/p][p]We've also improved the overall crafting experience. The crafting menu now shows how many of each item you already own, helping avoid unnecessary duplicates. When salvaging items, a confirmation message appears if your storage is full, so resources won’t be lost by accident.[/p][p][/p][h3]Training Camp[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/3c849eae84cc0d539e2c0ae9d3d9717ca3dfa332.png"][/img][/p][p]The story progression received a few updates as well. Since the early game was mainly focused on building the first camp, switching straight into combat at the Training Camp felt a bit disconnected. To address this, the Training Camp now offers two parallel progression paths. One follows the original route with the Obstacle Course and Combat Training. The new one centers around helping with building and crafting tasks. You can assist Training Camp members such as the Quartermaster or Blacksmith by making various items for the camp and earn special rewards in return. This gives you more freedom to choose how you want to progress.[/p][p]Trading has also been unlocked, allowing you to sell and purchase goods from Training Camp vendors.[/p][p]Another new feature is the ability to give gifts to key characters at the camp. These can be found while exploring the world and gifted when you return. Improving someone’s approval brings various benefits, such as better trading prices, and in future updates, characters with high approval will become available for faction recruitment.[/p][p]Several existing quests were improved as well. The Combat Training quest now provides a shield to make completing it with blunt weapons easier, and ranged weapons automatically come with ammunition. A free skill point is also given during training to unlock a Strong Attack ability.[/p][p]Quest experience rewards have been increased across the board, and recommended levels were adjusted to make progression feel smoother.[/p][p][/p][h3]Squads[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/9c1a7ea7a0a1f8feb580212fefda53c4cdbe5b2b.png"][/img][/p][p]The squad system has been made more flexible. After unlocking squads through story progression, you can now choose between [b]Solo[/b] and [b]Party[/b] modes. Solo mode is for those who prefer to play with just one character and don’t want to switch between others. To support this playstyle, the main character receives a set of stat bonuses, including increased Stamina, and Focus, faster buildup of status effects, and damage reduction.[/p][p]If you prefer to manage a full group, Party mode keeps things as they were in previous versions, with access to multiple characters and the ability to switch between them freely.[/p][p][/p][h3]Character Customization[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/7277b29c72990689438427fba0ad534e9c893262.png"][/img][/p][p]Character customization has received several updates. A new Appearance tab has been added to the Inventory menu, letting you change how your gear looks without any relation to its stats. Once you discover a piece of equipment, its visual style becomes available and can be applied to the corresponding gear slot, regardless of what you currently have equipped. Equipment colors can also be freely adjusted, giving you more control over your character’s look.[/p][p]Character equipment is now also displayed during the character selection screen. Old characters need to be resaved for this to take effect.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]That wraps up today’s overview of what’s new in this version. There are many more fixes, tweaks, and smaller changes not covered here, so be sure to check out [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2074620/view/515217056009815932"]the full patch notes[/url] for all the details.[/p][p]As always, thank you for your continued support and for helping us test and shape the game. We’re excited to hear your feedback and hope you enjoy everything we’ve added. See you in the next update![/p]

notes.title: Ars Notoria Playtest Returns
notes.notes: [p]It’s been a while since our last playtest, and we’re thrilled to open the gates again! Over the past few months, we’ve focused on improving the early-game experience, fixing bugs, and making quality-of-life adjustments based on your feedback.[/p][p]This new playtest brings a host of updates, fixes, and new content. Whether you’re returning to see what’s new or jumping in for the first time, we can’t wait to hear what you think.[/p][p]If you’ve participated in a previous Ars Notoria playtest, you can download and launch the new build from your library. If this is your first time, simply click the “Request Access” button on the Steam store page — you’ll receive an email notification once you’ve been added to the playtest.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/5a11a05c21f5f2538017010f5aa539184b65f95a.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]🕒 [b]The playtest will be live from August 4 to August 12, [/b]featuring version [b]v0.3.1.3[/b].[/p][p]Versions 0.3.1.0 to 0.3.1.3 include improvements to tutorials, exploration, and magic. We’ve added new quests, items, and [b]dungeon rewards[/b], [b]reworked and simplified resource gathering tools[/b], and enhanced squad and faction systems.[/p][p]Here’s the full changelog covering Build 0.3.1.0 through 0.3.1.3.[/p][p][/p][h2]Build 0.3.1.0[/h2][h3]Tutorials[/h3][list][*][p]Added an in-game guide.[/p][/*][*][p]The in-game guide includes the updated building unlock progression and supports shortcuts. Clicking a recipe icon will open it directly in the Crafting or Building menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Resource processing and automatization tutorials are now available earlier during the Training Camp.[/p][/*][*][p]The Magic Basics tutorial quest now rewards the Forsworn Attire crafting recipe upon completion.[/p][/*][*][p]The Magic Basics tutorial can now also be obtained by defeating an Enthralled enemy.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the notification for completing the Magic Basics tutorial could appear multiple times.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where small shrubs were not counted toward completing an objective in the Harvesting Resources tutorial.[/p][/*][/list][h3]Quests[/h3][list][*][p][b]Added a new main quest for the Quartermaster.[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where loading a backup from the start of the game might not trigger the initial tutorial quest.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the Sleeping status effect might not be removed after a dialogue with a guard patrol.[/p][/*][/list][h3]Exploration[/h3][list][*][p]Added random enemy encounters on Normal and Survival difficulties. notes.title: Ars Notoria Eastern Game Fest Playtest Concludes — Thank You for Joining Us
notes.notes:
[h2]Ars Notoria Playtest Concludes[/h2]

The test has officially ended at 10:00 UTC. We deeply appreciate every piece of feedback and suggestion you've shared during this period — your input plays a crucial role in helping us improve the game. The development team will carefully review all feedback and work hard to deliver a better Ars Notoria in the future.

We look forward to seeing you again in the next test!

Thank you all for your patience and support!

[b]Playtest Period[/b]
April 24, 2:00 AM – May 6 (PDT)

[b]Feedback & Bug Hunt Event[/b]
To thank you for participating, we’ll be giving away serveal full release keys to the most helpful bug reporters or feedback providers!
English feedback will be collected in our #playtest-bug-reports channel on Discord.
For full event details, please join our [url=https://discord.gg/g2HaVSdy6H]official Discord[/url].

If you’re interested in joining the PlayTest, we invite you to fill out the registration form. Eligible players will be contacted promptly. You can also sign up for the Playtest through Steam’s “Request Access” feature. However, please note that we are unable to control which players get selected via the Steam platform.
[url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc2kQ1yFc0QVi5bFMOq92d6glksHjSUIp-KWgypvSIvIR-1tA/viewform?]Registration Form[/url]

[h2]Build Update[/h2]
[h3]Story[/h3]
[list]
[*] Unlocked the main story arc for the Training Camp.
[/list]
[h3]Tutorials[/h3]
[list]
[*] The "Setting Up Camp" tutorial has now been changed to a main quest, as it provides a transition to the Training Camp quest line.
[*] Fixed an issue where tutorial windows might not appear in certain cases.
[*] Fixed an issue where loading a game with a tutorial quest in progress would redisplay the tutorial window.
[/list]
[h3]World[/h3]
[list]
[*] Unlocked the Training Camp location and the surrounding areas in the Woodlands.
[*] Added Waystones, which can be used as fast travel points throughout the game world.
[*] Added Notice Boards that offer optional side quests.
[*] The respawn point is now available for fast travel from anywhere on the map when fast travel is enabled in the server settings. 
[*] Fast travel cannot be used while in combat, mounted, or inside a dungeon or building.
[*] Added faction reputation system.
[/list]
[h3]Characters[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added Attack Speed character stat.
[*] Added Approval mechanics for NPCs.
[*] Added daily routines for NPCs.
[*] Unlocked character-switching mechanics.
[*] Unlocked combat classes.
[*] The appearance of generated NPCs is now saved across game worlds and synchronized between the host and clients.
[*] Fixed an issue where the interaction tooltip was displayed for NPCs without available dialogue.
[/list]
[h3]Multiplayer[/h3]
[list]
[*] Reworked multiplayer synchronization for pre-built containers and items. Their contents are now properly shared between the host and clients.
[*] Fixed an issue where dead bodies in the Destroyed Village were not displayed for clients.
[*] Fixed an issue where moving containers for clients might cause them to appear frozen in mid-air.
[*] Fixed an issue where campfires might not display fire effects for clients.
[/list]
[h3]Server Settings[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added an option to customize fast travel settings. The available modes are:
[olist]
[*] Default - Fast travel is only allowed when interacting with an activated waystone.
[*] Global - Fast travel is allowed from anywhere in the game world to a selected waystone.
[*] Disabled - Waystones cannot be activated, and fast travel is unavailable.
[/olist][/list]
[h3]Save Games[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added an option to load game world backups.
[*] Added an option to restore backups for character saves with missing or invalid data.
[*] Added visual indicators for character save files that contain invalid data.
[*] Fixed an issue where creating a new character in an existing world could use an incorrect save slot.
[/list]
[h3]Combat[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added an option to block while using ranged weapons. Holding Alt + RMB activates blocking.
[*] Fixed an issue where aiming with ranged weapons could be interrupted near campfires.
[/list]
[h3]Resources[/h3]
[list]
[*] Small shrubs can now be destroyed and will provide a bit of softwood.
[*] Increased manual harvesting speed for basic trees and resource deposits by 30–50%.
[*] Rebalanced harvesting skill experience gain by increasing experience requirements for higher levels.
[/list]
[h3]Items[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added a new item type, Recipes, which can be used to unlock crafting and cooking recipes.
[*] Added craftable and refillable Healing Potions.
[*] Added a new unique armor set, the Redthorn Armor. It is awarded for outstanding achievements during training at the camp.
[*] Improved the physics interactions of pickable items.
[*] Fixed an issue where the amount of gold found in containers could be lower than intended.
[/list]
[h3]Customization[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added beards and moustaches.
[*] Added face and body tattoos.
[*] Improved eye textures.
[*] Fixed an issue where default clothing and hair colors could display incorrect values when returning to the Character Selection menu.
[*] Fixed an issue where canceling new character creation caused the selected character's appearance to display incorrectly.
[*] Fixed an issue where customization slider values might not reset to default when creating a new character after selecting an existing one.
[*] Fixed an issue where modifications to an existing character's appearance might not be applied.
[/list]
[h3]User Interface[/h3]
[list]
[*] Unlocked the Character tab in the Journal.
[*] Added a "Travel to Respawn" button to the Map menu.
[*] Fixed an issue where the map and minimap had a lower resolution than intended.
[*] Fixed an issue where a selected completed quest might be highlighted incorrectly in the Quest Journal.
[*] Fixed an issue where completed quest objectives may have incorrect formatting after loading the game.
[*] Fixed an issue where the final objective of a skipped quest was incorrectly marked as in progress after loading the game.
[*] Various formatting fixes for the dialogue UI.
[/list]
[h3]Status Effects[/h3]
[list]
[*] Diseases can now be cured by the Healer at the Training Camp.
[/list]
[h3]Other[/h3]

Greetings!
We’re thrilled to announce that Ars Notoria will be showcased at the Eastern Game Fest! This event marks an exciting opportunity for players to dive into the mystical world we’ve been refining since our last playtest.

[h3]What’s New?[/h3]
Since our previous test, we’ve implemented numerous optimizations and gameplay enhancements based on community feedback. Today, we’re proud to reveal that Ars Notoria will host a limited-time PlayTest during the Eastern Game Fest!

[h3]PlayTest Details & Key Updates[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Test Period[/b]
April 23rd – May 6th (PDT)

[*] [b]How to Participate[/b]
If you’re interested in joining the PlayTest, we invite you to fill out the registration form. Eligible players will be contacted promptly. You can also sign up for the Playtest through Steam’s “Request Access” feature. However, please note that we are unable to control which players get selected via the Steam platform. Registration Form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc2kQ1yFc0QVi5bFMOq92d6glksHjSUIp-KWgypvSIvIR-1tA/viewform?


[*] [b]Major Additions & Improvements[/b]

[b]Training Camp Story Arc[/b]
A brand-new storyline set in the Training Camp is now available. It introduces the Holy Guard faction, along with unique NPCs, quests, and an expanded area for exploration. We've also added daily routines for most characters, new dialogues, and additional interaction options to enrich the experience.

[b]Character Switching Mechanics[/b]
Progressing through the main Training Camp quests unlocks new mechanics that let you form a squad of up to four characters, allowing you to switch between them freely—both during combat and while exploring.

[b]Combat Classes[/b]
After completing basic combat training at the camp, you'll gain access to six combat classes. These classes offer new ways to develop and customize your character's abilities and playstyle.

[b]Waystones[/b]
Waystones are magical structures that enable fast travel between locations. We've also added an option to return to your selected respawn point via the World Map. Fast travel is enabled by default, but customizable settings are available when starting a new game, allowing you to disable or adjust how it functions.

[b]Notice Boards[/b]
Found in settlements and outposts, notice boards offer access to side quests given by nearby NPCs.

[b]Reputation & Approval Systems[/b]
With the introduction of the Holy Guard faction and new characters, we’ve implemented faction reputation and character approval systems. These affect faction management progression and influence character recruitment.

[b]Quality-of-Life Improvements[/b]
Based on feedback from previous testing phases, we’ve added several improvements to enhance gameplay, including:
1. The ability to block enemy attacks while using ranged weapons
2. Map indicators for hard-to-find quest objectives
3. The option to harvest wood from small shrubs
4. Increased speed for manual resource gathering
5. Improved stability and the ability to load backup saves of your game world

[b]Character Customization[/b]
The new version offers expanded character customization options, including beards, mustaches, and face and body tattoos.

[b]New Items and Equipment[/b]
The Training Camp also introduces new items and rewards. You can also earn a unique armor set by completing optional objectives during training quests.
[/list]

Join the Mystical Journey!
This PlayTest offers a chance to experience Ars Notoria’s evolving world firsthand. Whether you’re a returning player or a newcomer, your feedback will shape the path to perfection.
Thank you for your support, and see you at the Eastern Game Fest! 
Join our official Disocord: https://discord.gg/bYNb6kmw

— The Ars Notoria Dev Team

Hi everyone!
 
The second multiplayer test of Ars Notoria ended on February 10th at 10:30 AM UTC. We sincerely thank you for exploring this world, battling its dangers, and sharing your insights with us.

Your feedback has been instrumental in shaping the future of Ars Notoria. Next, we will focus on incorporating the valuable suggestions we've gathered and optimizing the game. Once these updates are nearing completion, we will share them with you in our upcoming announcements.

If you’ve enjoyed your time in this world, please add the game to your wishlist—your support fuels our journey forward.

Thank you for being part of this tale, and stay tuned for updates!

————————————————————————————

[h3]Original announcement[/h3]

Hey everyone!

We haven’t spoken for a while, but it doesn't mean we haven't been working on optimizing new content of Ars Notoria. Now we’re thrilled to announce that the second round of multiplayer testing is about to begin. Want to join the adventure? Fill out the [url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd6oTB6M7x4SC7tDGp5CqVOHmVDpxJp4pO2kUDQhI99RmjxMQ/viewform?usp=sharing]questionnaire[/url] to participate.

The latest update is here, filled with new content, challenges, and quality-of-life improvements. We hope you'll grab your gear, gather your allies, and explore what’s new.

[h3]The Dark Forest Beckons: Expanded Exploration[/h3]
We invite you to venture deeper into the mysterious Dark Forest. Previously, only a portion of this zone was accessible, but now, the entire Dark Forest awaits your exploration. Discover new Places of Interest, such as Altars for summoning Enthralled creatures, the eerie Crypts filled with skeletons and undead spiders, and the treacherous Spider Nests. Explore perilous dungeons, face a variety of new enemies, and uncover hidden secrets. Every corner of the Dark Forest is designed to challenge the brave and reward the curious.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/1e0d958668efb0acff77eb3bf1b2406f3ed04a07.png[/img]

[h3]Forge, Form, Flourish: New Research Tools[/h3]
For base-building enthusiasts, we’ve added a new research stations for the Engineering profession.
Get ready to supercharge your faction’s resource harvesting and management! This update brings shiny new Engineering tools, unlocking a treasure trove of technologies to boost your resource management. With these powerful upgrades, you'll be improving your base like a true mastermind!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/4a3bb6156d1975453215935e084c260106075a76.png[/img]

[h3]New Enemies: Undead Spiders lurking in the Dark Forest[/h3]
We’ve got a creepy new surprise for you in the Dark Forest: Undead Spiders!
That’s right, the Dark Forest just got spookier. Prepare yourselves for three terrifying new types of eight-legged nightmares, straight from your worst arachnid nightmares:
1. Biters – Fast, grotesque undead spiders with skull-like bodies and glowing eyes. They may not be tough individually, but their swarming speed makes them deadly.
2. Crawlers – Massive, armored spiders with human skulls fused into their bodies. They have a venomous stinger that paralyzes foes, making them a real threat in tight spaces.
3. Spinners – Enormous, magical spiders that shoot webs with pinpoint accuracy. Strong and agile, they can trap you in their webs before delivering a crushing blow.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/b1d9e8aa472f8927aafdcdbd3d86b229cf882679.png[/img]

[h3]Flatter Terrain: Perfect Spots for Your New Base![/h3]
We’ve rolled out some spacious new flat terrain patches—perfect for building your dream base right near the starting zone, or anywhere else you fancy! Oh, and the Dark Forest biome just got a makeover too, with basic resources like stone and iron ore popping up, plus a few extra surprises. Time to get building and resource-hunting!

[h3]Empower Your Heroine: Female Character Customization[/h3]
We’re excited to announce that female character customization is now available! Tailor your warrior's look with a variety of options, from hairstyles and facial features. Express yourself in the harsh world of survival like never before. Whether you’re crafting, fighting, or leading your faction, do it with style.

notes.notes:
Hi, everyone!

With the release of the Faction Management update (version 0.1.0.4), we have successfully integrated and tested most of the core single-player systems. Moving forward, our focus will shift toward preparing for multiplayer mode testing. notes.title: Magic System Update
notes.notes:
Hi everyone!

We've uploaded the demo update that adds the magic system to the game. It includes the new Enchanter crafting class with the corresponding equipment. There are also new variations of enemies that have elemental magic and drop spellcrafting materials when defeated.

We plan to add more types of spells and their modifications in the upcoming patches, including summoning magic.

Here is the full list of changes in the update:

[h3]Magic System[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added six Magic Arts:
[olist]
[*] Ars Goetia - fire magic that is focused on attacking spells and boosting the character's parameters.
[*] Ars Theurgia - frost magic that is focused on defensive spells and slowing enemies.
[*] Ars Paulina - poison magic that is focused on dealing damage over time and debilitating enemies.
[*] Ars Almadel - lightning magic that is focused on high burst damage and AoE spells.
[*] Ars Necromia - chaos magic that is focused on summoning and durability spells.
[*] Ars Notoria - holy magic that is focused on healing, dispelling, and utility spells.
[/olist]
[*] Added basic craftable and customizable spells for all Magic Arts.
[*] Added perks unlocked by leveling Magic Arts. They can provide various bonuses to selected spells.
[*] Added a Magic Sigil which allows slotting spells and perks to improve their efficiency.
[*] Added adjustable spell parameters:
[olist]
[*] Intensity - each point changes parameters like spell damage, minion strength, or barrier amount by 5%.
[*] Magnitude - each point changes parameters like maximum projectile range, size, or AoE by 10%.
[*] Momentum - each point changes parameters like speed, duration, or tick rate by 10%.
[*] Efficiency - each point changes parameters like spell cost by 7.5%.
[/olist]
[*] Added materials for spell crafting: Soul Shards, Glyphs, and Runestones.
[/list]
[h3]Combat[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added a hotkey for toggling aiming mode, defaulted to "F" button. It can be remapped in the Settings. 
This feature enables aiming mode even when using melee weapons, making it useful for spell casting.
[*] Increased the base Focus Regeneration value from 0.3 to 0.8 FP/sec.
[*] Significantly reduced the casting delay for Strong Attacks, making them execute almost immediately.
[*] Further reduced delays after executing Fast Attacks by 0.1 to 0.2 seconds.
[*] Parrying can now also be activated while blocking by pressing RMB again. The parrying window has been increased.
[*] Increased the base value of Physical and Elemental Block from 30% to 50%.
[*] Removed staggering from enemy Fast Attacks.
[*] Added buildup status effects:
[olist]
[*] Bleeding - Periodically deals damage based on the target's current health and reduces health regeneration.
[*] Stunned - Stuns the target for a short period of time and increases the poise damage.
[*] Ruptured - The target receives damage while moving, which scales based on the distance traveled.
[*] Staggered - Knocks down the target for a short period of time and reduces the resistance to staggering.
[*] Burning - Deals damage over time and increases delays between enemy attacks.
[*] Frozen - Freezes the target for a short period of time and then slows down attack and movement speed.
[*] Poisoned - Reduces enemy damage and inflicts damage that gradually increases over time.
[*] Shocked - Increases the critical hit chance against the target and slows down stamina and focus regeneration.
[*] Frightened - The enemy has reduced physical resistances and a chance to fumble an attack, dealing only half of the damage.
[*] Purged - Removes a positive effect from the target and temporarily increases all damage received.
[/olist]
[*] Added immunity to bleeding for Undead enemies.
[*] Fixed an issue where the enemy Charge attack might not be executed.
[*] Fixed an issue where attacks or hotkeys might not work after being staggered by an enemy in some cases.
[*] Fixed an issue where enemy attacks could consume more stamina than intended.
[*] Fixed an issue where negative resistances might not increase the damage received.
[*] Fixed an issue where enemy rotation might be incorrect while casting spells.
[/list]
[h3]Enemies[/h3]

notes.title: Demo Build 0.1.0.2c
notes.notes:

[/list]

[list]

Ammunition replaces Stamina cost for ranged abilities when enabled.
At the moment, it's an experimental feature and can be toggled in the settings.
[*] Added second and third combo moves for all melee default attacks: Sword, Blunt Weapon, and Polearm.
[*] Added a parry ability for Unarmed combat.
[*] Added a visual indicator to show when the enemy attack can be parried. It can be toggled on and off in the Settings menu.
[*] Added a visual indicator for strong and charge enemy attacks that cannot be parried and immobilize the character on hit. It can be toggled on and off in the Settings menu.
[*] Added a knockdown effect to successful parries.
[*] Character movement speed is now preserved after dodging.
[*] Changed the first combo move for Sword, Blunt Weapon, and Polearm default attacks.
[*] When only the first combo ability is learned, it will automatically transition into the default combo. 
When two or more combo abilities are learned, they will be used in a cycle without switching to the default one (the same way it worked before). 
This change is aimed to prevent situations where the character could only use a single attack and to make combat more fluid.
[*] Changed Suppression rifle ability damage type from Ballistic to Piercing.
[*] Changed Bayonet Attack rifle ability damage type from Piercing to Slashing.
[*] Changed default rifle attack damage type from Ballistic to Piercing.
[*] Increased damage of Parry attacks by 100% and effect buildup by 50%.
[*] Reduced transition time from Sidestep/Evade to combat abilities by 0.3 seconds.
[*] Reduced transition time from combat abilities to Sidestep/Evade by 0.3-0.8 seconds, depending on the ability length.
[*] Adjusted the animation length and speed of Sidestep abilities to make them more consistent.
[*] Improved bullet tracing against moving targets.
[*] Increased the physical block bonus for the Iron Buckler item from 3-6% to 10-20% and added an extra armor affix.
[*] Fixed an issue where the aiming target lock might be active when there were no combat targets.
[*] Fixed an issue where some default attacks didn't apply effect buildup.
[*] Fixed an issue where Guard tooltip was shown instead of Aim when ranged weapons were equipped.

[list]
[*] Added a Strong Attack to Skeleton Mages.
[*] Adjusted timings of some enemy abilities.
[*] Increased the Strong Attack cooldown for foxes.
[*] Adjusted ground friction for rat bodies to reduce rolling on slopes.
[*] Fixed an issue where Bandit Thieves couldn't execute melee attacks in some cases.
[/list]

[list]

[*] Fixed an issue where horse equipment items could be unequipped after loading in some cases.

notes.title: Demo Build 0.1.0.2b
notes.notes:
Hi, everyone! We uploaded the 0.1.0.2b which includes a lot of bug fixes and other changes. It features a reworked tutorial system, with much more detailed explanations and videos. There are also improvements in almost all gameplay systems that are based on the feedback that we received since the demo launch.

We plan to release one more patch with fixes and quality-of-life improvements after this one, and then focus on content updates for the demo. The upcoming patch will include functionality to move existing build parts, an alternative inventory-based UI for the building menu, and more types of default weapon attacks.

The full list of changes in the current patch:

[h2]Demo Build 0.1.0.2b[/h2]

[h3]Tutorials[/h3]
[list]
[*] Reworked existing tutorials to a new format with videos and more detailed explanations.
[*] All tutorials are now presented in a fixed order for easier progression. The horse taming tutorial is still available separately upon discovering a wild horse.
[*] The Destroyed Village quest line unlocks only after completing or skipping the tutorials.
[/list]
[h3]Resources[/h3]
[list]
[*] Increased the guaranteed amount of rare resource pieces (clay, fuel, pigments, salts, precious ore) near deposits to 4-5.
[*] Increased the chance of finding common resource pieces (stone, iron ore) near deposits from 100%/50%/25% to 100%/100%/75%.
[*] Wild plants (fibers, herbs, crops) are now generated in groups of several plants instead of a single one.
[*] Holding E now allows to automatically continue resource harvesting.
[*] Rat pelts can now be used to produce leather.
[*] Added guaranteed herb and fiber resource spawns near the starting location.
[*] Fixed an issue where auto-equipping an axe might not work with bushes.
[*] Fixed an issue where resource pieces might not spawn near the character after loading the game.
[*] Fixed an issue where a tool wasn't auto-equipped when holding a weapon.
[*] Fixed an issue where trees could regrow through obstacles in some cases.
[*] Fixed an issue where the type of resource deposit could change after an update or alterations to the world seed value.
[*] Fixed an issue where saplings could respawn if they were harvested using the Interact button before they grew.
[*] Fixed an issue where resource deposit pieces and minimap icons could sometimes become hidden when the character was close.
[/list]
[h3]Environment[/h3]
[list]
[*] Replaced forest grass meshes with smaller ones with better optimization. This change aims to improve both visibility and performance.
